name: Leleākūhonua
axesStatus: Equal axes at the occultation radius, which assumes a circular outline.
credit: Buie et al. (2020), The Astronomical Journal 159, 230: radius 110 +14/−10 km from the 2018 October 20 stellar occultation, assuming a circular profile
shapeMeaning: Sphere of radius 110 km (+14/−10 km), from one detection and one nearby non-detection of the 2018 October 20 stellar occultation (Buie et al. 2020). The radius assumes a circular outline; the shape is not measured.
orientationMeaning: Illustrative ICRF north pole, arbitrary prime meridian and phase; no spin pole is published.
surfaceMeaning: Unmapped surface: the standard grid is a coordinate aid, not observed color or terrain.
introduction: Leleākūhonua never comes closer to the Sun than about 65 au, and its orbit reaches beyond 2,500 au. Its discoverers reported it as the third known member of the inner Oort cloud.
card: Found in 2015; its orbit reaches more than 2,500 au from the Sun.
datasetSummary: A sphere of radius 110 km, measured in a 2018 stellar occultation assuming a circular outline.

textCitations.label: JPL Small-Body Database
